question.question_text: Does UMG Article 1 (occupations et utilisations du sol interdites) prohibit constructions à destination d'habitation?
likely_source_documents: plu_reglement: Zone UMG, ARTICLE 1 (p. 319 printed / pdf p. 320)
question.rationale: Admissibility of the residential use is the gating question for both buildings. The Article 1 list (agricultural/forestry, entrepôt, caravans, camping, RLL, villages de vacances) does not appear to include habitation, but this must be confirmed from text.

answer.answer_text: No. UMG Article 1 does not prohibit constructions à destination d'habitation. The prohibited list covers agricultural/forestry and entrepôt constructions (c-01)[Les constructions, ouvrages ou travaux à destination d'exploitation agricole ou forestière et d'entrepôt]. The only item in that list that refers to habitation is the caravan used as housing (c-02)[L'installation d'une caravane à usage d'habitation]. The zone description states that habitation is an intended use (c-03)[des constructions à destination d'habitation, au bénéfice des étudiants, des chercheurs, et des familles].
answer.additional_context: The Article 1 prohibition on a caravan used as housing does not prohibit building habitation. Article 1 was read on printed page 319 (PDF page 320). Article 2 (printed page 320, PDF page 321) lists only conditional uses and does not address habitation, so Article 1 alone does not settle admissibility of the RSE or Résidence Jeunes Actifs buildings. The planner's list of prohibited uses matches the source text.

likely_source_documents: plu_reglement: Zone UMG, ARTICLE 2 (p. 320 printed / pdf p. 321)
question.rationale: Completes the admissibility determination. If habitation is neither prohibited (Q01) nor conditioned (Q02), it is admitted without specific conditions, which the zone introduction supports.

answer.answer_text: No. The UMG Article 2 list of uses admitted under conditions does not include constructions à destination d'habitation (c-01)[Article 2 lists affouillements et exhaussements, équipements techniques de réseaux, voiries et stationnements, and installations classées; no habitation item]. Article 1 prohibits only a caravane à usage d'habitation, not habitation buildings (c-02)[Sont interdites ... L'installation d'une caravane à usage d'habitation]. The zone introduction states that the zone is destined for habitation, but it is descriptive and is not an Article 2 admission (c-03)[constructions à destination d'habitation, au bénéfice des étudiants, des chercheurs, et des familles].
answer.discrepancy_note: The planner states that the zone introduction supports admission of habitation without specific conditions. The introduction (printed p. 319, PDF p. 320) says the zone is 'destinée à accueillir' habitation, but it is a descriptive statement, not an operative admission rule. The operative provisions are Article 1 (prohibitions) and Article 2 (conditional admissions). Article 2 does not list habitation, so the answer is no for the conditional-admission list. Whether habitation is admitted unconditionally rests on the absence of a prohibition plus the general admissibility rules, which this question does not resolve.
answer.additional_context: Article 2 is worded as 'Sont admises, sous conditions, les occupations et utilisations du sol suivantes' and the list is closed. Habitation therefore is not a conditional use under Article 2 in this text. The Article 1 prohibition covers only the caravane à usage d'habitation. Q01 and any unconditional-admission determination should be checked against the remaining zone rules, which were not examined here. question.rationale: Zone UL2 has a student-accommodation condition. The UMG text must be checked separately to confirm that no equivalent condition applies to the RSE.

answer.answer_text: No. UMG Article 2 attaches no condition to hébergement étudiant or to student residences. Its conditional list begins 'Sont admises, sous conditions, les occupations et utilisations du sol suivantes' and covers only affouillements/exhaussements, technical network equipment, and installations classées (c-01)[Sont admises, sous conditions, les occupations et utilisations du sol suivantes]. The UMG zone intro says the zone is for habitation 'au bénéfice des étudiants, des chercheurs, et des familles' (c-03)[des constructions à destination d'habitation, au bénéfice des étudiants, des chercheurs, et des familles]. The student-accommodation condition named in the planner rationale is in zone UL2 (Vallée), not UMG (c-04)[A l'hébergement étudiant et à la formation].
answer.additional_context: The planner's UL2 claim is confirmed, but UL2 belongs to the Vallée zone and does not transfer to UMG. The negative finding covers the full UMG Article 2 text (printed p.320 / pdf p.321). Any admissibility of habitation in UMG rests on the zone intro and the absence of a prohibition in Article 1, which is an interpretation not stated expressly in the text.

question.question_text: What is the maximum height in metres for constructions à destination principale d'habitation under UMG Article 10.2?
likely_source_documents: plu_reglement: Zone UMG, ARTICLE 10.2 (p. 325 printed / pdf p. 326)
question.rationale: Provides the height ceiling for the residential buildings if they are classified as habitation (Q03, Q04).

answer.answer_text: For constructions with a principal destination of habitation, UMG Article 10.2 limits height to 20 metres, with a maximum of R+5 storeys (c-01)[la hauteur maximale des constructions est limitée à 20 mètres, avec un nombre de niveaux limité à R+5]. Constructions with another destination are limited to 18 metres (c-02)[Pour les constructions ayant une autre destination : la hauteur maximale des constructions est limitée à 18 mètres]. Article 10 also requires projects to be compatible with the OAP (c-03)[Tout projet doit être compatible avec les orientations]. Height runs from the natural ground up to the ridge or acrotère, with technical works included, subject to the 10.1 exclusions (c-04)[ouvrages techniques compris].
answer.additional_context: The 20 m limit applies only if the building is classified as habitation. This answer does not resolve whether the RSE or the Résidence Jeunes Actifs falls under habitation, which depends on Q03 and Q04. Article 10.2 does not define habitation. The source text is on printed page 325 (PDF page 326).
